clue.text: An encounter where one easily won dear hearts, perhaps

definitions.text: An encounter where one easily won

parts.note: a loved one may be addressed as dear or love
hearts is one example of a card game, flagged by 'perhaps'

explanation.surface: A romantic meeting in which someone won affection without effort.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis, a game taken without the opponent winning a single point is the easiest possible win.

clue.text: This is the solution!

parts.note: the words a solver is reading are themselves the thing being described: a puzzle hint that is, wryly, offered as the answer

explanation.definitionFit: The printed line a solver reads is a crossword hint; here that hint names itself, so the word being asked for is its own description.

clue.text: Under you once, VAT's raised without full assent

indicators.note: in a down entry the reversed tubs sits below the old form of you

parts.note: ye is an old form of you

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising the word tubs reads it from the bottom up, backwards

parts.note: vats are tubs, and the 's makes it plural

explanation.surface: An old complaint about the tax going up, voiced with only half-hearted agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT looks like the British sales tax, but it is a large vessel; in a down entry 'raised' reads it upwards, and 'Under' places it below the archaic pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'yes, but' agrees in principle while holding back, so it is grudging, partial agreement.

clue.text: Spooner's journo under Prohibition gets a shot

indicators.note: Spooner, famous for swapping the opening sounds of words, signals a Spoonerism

parts.note: a hack is a jobbing journalist
something under a prohibition is banned

explanation.surface: A reporter working in the Prohibition era lands a big story.
explanation.walkthrough: Say HACK BANNED with the opening sounds swapped and you get BACK HANNED, which sounds like the tennis stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: A backhand is a tennis stroke played with the back of the hand facing the ball.

clue.text: Prepare pear, eat and pay fruit producer

indicators.note: to prepare food is to work it into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions to get some fruit ready, eat it, and pay for it.
explanation.definitionFit: The tree that bears papaya fruit is literally a producer of fruit.

clue.text: Young woman takes shot in international

indicators.note: the young woman's word takes in, or holds, the shot's word

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl or young woman
a lob is a high tennis shot over the opponent

explanation.surface: A young woman plays a shot in an international match.
explanation.definitionFit: Global and international both describe something spanning many nations.

clue.text: Mixed doubles interrupted by intro from Rolling Stones

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are broken into by the next piece
mixed means jumbled, so these letters are put in a new order
the introduction to a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A mixed doubles tennis match is interrupted when the Rolling Stones come on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed' rearranges DOUBLES into BOULDES; the first letter of 'Rolling' interrupts it.
explanation.definitionFit: Boulders are large rocks, so they are big stones.

clue.text: Start, say, to analyse a clue: for example, 'not dense'

indicators.note: the start of the word say is its opening letter

parts.note: to parse is to break a sentence, or a clue, down grammatically

explanation.surface: Advice to a solver: start by breaking down the clue, rather than being dense.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sparse is thinly spread, the opposite of thick or crowded.

clue.text: Boatman gets into real trouble being productive in the field

indicators.note: the sailor's letters go inside the other piece
in trouble means disturbed, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: AB, an able seaman, is a boatman; Boatman is also the setter

explanation.surface: The setter finds himself in real difficulty while out working the land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges REAL into ARLE, and AB 'gets into' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Arable land is fit for ploughing and growing crops, so its fields yield harvests.

clue.text: Lose control through unforced error

indicators.note: the answer runs through the clue words, spanning both of them

explanation.surface: A tennis player's mistake without pressure costs them their grip on the match.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede is to give up or surrender power, territory or advantage.

clue.text: British Miss married a business school type, a snake

parts.note: to miss something is to lack it
an MBA is the business school degree, and by extension someone holding it

explanation.surface: A British woman marries a business graduate who turns out to be a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a woman's title; it is the verb, to lack.
explanation.definitionFit: The black mamba is a fast, highly venomous African serpent.

clue.text: Frequently found with grass, say, and dismissed

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, giving one that sounds the same

parts.note: a tennis court is often a grass court, so the word that frequently accompanies grass is court

explanation.surface: Something often discovered with marijuana, leading to a dismissal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' looks like the drug or an informer; it is a tennis surface, as at Wimbledon. In non-rhotic British speech court and the answer sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a batter out from a catch is dismissed that way, so it is a mode of dismissal.

clue.text: After middle age (51), metal on US mobiles affects brain matter

indicators.note: the Roman numeral comes after the middle letter
the middle of the word age is its centre letter

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium, a metal
Americans call mobile phones cells or cellphones

explanation.surface: Past fifty, heavy metal on mobile phones takes its toll on the brain.
explanation.definitionFit: Glial cells are the support cells of the nervous system, a large part of the brain's tissue.

clue.text: New balls — and ace is not insurmountable

indicators.note: making something new from these letters means rearranging them

explanation.surface: With fresh tennis balls and an ace, the deficit can be overcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scalable can be climbed, so it is a height or obstacle that can be got over.

clue.text: Spenser's miscalled on return of serve

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to serve something is to deliver it

explanation.surface: The poet Spenser bad-mouthed on a returned serve.
explanation.walkthrough: Edmund Spenser, Elizabethan poet, used miscall to mean abuse or slander; 'Spenser's' marks the archaic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In Spenser's English, to miscall someone was to abuse them by name, to rail at them.

clue.text: Objects to set in tie-break

indicators.note: to break something is to smash it apart, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A player protests at the set going to a tie-break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Objects' looks like a verb; it is a noun. 'break' rearranges SET, IN and TIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Entities are things that exist in their own right, as are objects.

clue.text: Dread getting beaten up taking empty subways where one lives

indicators.note: beaten up means knocked about, so these letters are jumbled
emptying a word removes everything between its outermost letters

explanation.surface: Fear of being mugged when walking through deserted underpasses near home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting beaten up' rearranges DREAD into ADDRE; empty 'subways' leaves SS.
explanation.definitionFit: Your street address locates your home, so it names where you are living.

clue.text: Great shot in middle of singles

parts.note: a smash is a hard overhead tennis shot

indicators.note: the centre of a seven-letter word is its fourth letter

explanation.surface: A fine stroke played midway through a singles match.
explanation.definitionFit: Smashing is informal British for excellent or terrific.

clue.text: Change ends or states monotonously

indicators.note: changing the letters means moving them into another order

explanation.surface: Tennis players change ends, or an umpire announces the score in a flat voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change ends' looks like the tennis switchover; 'Change' rearranges ENDS and OR.
explanation.definitionFit: To drone on is to speak in a dull, unvarying tone.

clue.text: Perhaps Moore curls topspin

indicators.note: spinning sends the letters round into a new order

explanation.surface: A player named Moore applies curling topspin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spin' is the end of 'topspin', and rearranges CURLS and TOP. Henry Moore was a British artist known for large bronze figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Moore is an example of a maker of statues, flagged by 'Perhaps'.

clue.text: Badger cull halted initially as college league takes victory

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of the two words
the league's word takes the victory's letter inside it

parts.note: the Ivy League is a group of elite US universities

explanation.surface: A badger cull is halted after the Ivy League wins a case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badger' looks like the animal; it is the verb to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger and to chivvy both mean to nag or harass someone into acting.

clue.text: US authority scorned rather than Boatman retreating inside

indicators.note: the reversed word goes inside the other piece

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: retreating goes back, so the setter's word is read in reverse

parts.note: Boatman is the setter, who refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: An American authority is despised, more so than the setter, who backs away.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by their pseudonym, so 'Boatman' stands for the first-person pronoun, which is 'retreating' and goes 'inside'.
explanation.definitionFit: In US slang, 'the Man' is the establishment or authority figure, resented by those it controls.

clue.text: Match point lost, even as it is creating surprises

indicators.note: losing the point removes that letter

parts.note: a twin is a match, one of a pair
N, north, is a point of the compass

indicators.note: the even letters of the words are the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: A match point is lost, as it is, surprising everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match point' reads as the tennis term; it is TWIN less N.
explanation.definitionFit: Plot twists are unexpected turns, things that take you by surprise.

clue.text: First of doubles with quashed serve in it against amateurs

indicators.note: the first of the word doubles is its opening letter
the let goes inside the word it

parts.note: in tennis a let is a serve that is voided and replayed
anti means against

explanation.surface: In doubles, a voided serve gets called against the amateur players.
explanation.definitionFit: Dilettanti dabble in the arts without professional commitment, like amateurs.

clue.text: Heads out of danger zone, hunting out a beast

indicators.note: the heads of the words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: Leading a hunt out of a danger zone, chasing an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dzho is a Himalayan cross between a yak and a cow, a farm animal.

clue.text: Show of emotion, perhaps missing sprint for shot

indicators.note: missing means the sprint's word is taken away

parts.note: a teardrop is one sign of feeling, flagged by 'perhaps'
to tear is to run very fast

explanation.surface: An emotional player, perhaps, is unable to run for a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop shot is a soft tennis stroke that lands just over the net.

clue.text: Emerge as first woman to take on half-volley

indicators.note: the first woman's name takes on, or holds, the other piece

parts.note: Eve is the first woman in Genesis

indicators.note: half of the six-letter word is its first three letters

explanation.surface: The first woman on court plays a half-volley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-volley' reads as the tennis stroke, but 'half' takes the front three letters of 'volley'.
explanation.definitionFit: To evolve is to develop gradually, so new forms come into being.

clue.text: Kindness at a tense moment in match?

parts.note: a set is a group of a kind, a class of things
a ness is a headland, as is a point

explanation.surface: A display of kindness at a tense point in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Set point is the stage when one more point wins a set, a moment of high tension.
